title: How deep is the sea? The ocean floor, its trenches and seamounts, on one map
excerpt: A map of the floor of the whole ocean, sharp from ocean basins to seamounts. The average sea floor lies 3,675 m down, 74% of it is abyssal, the Challenger Deep would hide Everest with 2,086 m to spare, and only 28.7% of the floor is mapped to modern standards.
seo_description: An interactive world map of ocean depth, with shaded sea floor relief, the deepest trenches, seamounts and how little of the floor is mapped.
header_alt: Title card reading 'How deep is the sea?' in black on pale grey, with the line: the average sea floor lies 3,675 m down; the deepest place, 10,935 m, would hide Everest with 2,086 m to spare. Beside it a world map in the Equal Earth projection with sandy land and a sea floor shaded from pale turquoise shelves to deep navy plains and dark trenches.
